subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up (PayWise)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@paywise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up (PayWise)

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the encryption and key management items we discussed:

1) PII & data handling
- We can disable request/response logging for routes that carry sensitive PII, or enable tokenization/pseudonymization before persisting.
- Default data retention for request logs is 90 days; retention windows can be shortened per account.

2) Encryption in-transit & at-rest
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ for all connections with mutual TLS available for Private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 (AES-GCM where applicable) for model artifacts and persisted snapshot data.

3) Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)
- Hosted: we support CMKs via AWS KMS and GCP KMS (imported keys or KMS-managed).
- Dedicated/Private: support for CloudHSM and customer HSMs via Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) pattern; can integrate with on-prem HSMs in Private deployments.
- Key rotation/rotation policies: we support rotation schedules and can configure automatic rotation or manual rotation workflows.

4) Compliance & attestations
- We'll share our SOC 2 report and KMS provider attestation. For FIPS 140-2/140-3, that depends on the underlying KMS/HSM provider — we can surface options that are FIPS-compliant.

Next steps:
- I will share the SOC2 and KMS options PDF (attached).
- Could we set up a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra/security team? Dev will join to walk the integration steps and sample config.
- Please send any specific compliance requirements (FIPS, data residency by country, required retention windows) so we can prepare answers and a short mutual action plan.

Proposed times: Tue 3/2 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 3/3 14:00–14:45 PT. Let me know what works or share a Cal link.

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_Options.pdf, SOC2_Audit_Report.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Amit Shah <amit@paywise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@paywise.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up (PayWise)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Can you share the sample KMS integration steps (ideally AWS and GCP examples) and an example of how key rotation is handled from our side vs. Redwood's side?
- Does Redwood support hardware-backed keys (HSM) that are provisioned on-prem? Our security team is specifically asking about FIPS 140-2 attestations for the entire key lifecycle.
- For data residency: we need guarantees that customer data (including logs if enabled) can be kept in us-east-1 or in eu-west-1 if we choose. Are there any limitations for model serving in specific regions?

We'll review the attachments, but if you can provide the KMS integration sample and propose times for the deep-dive, we can pull in our security lead.

— Amit

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-28T11:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up (PayWise)

Marissa — good notes. A few suggested clarifications to send to the customer: \

- KMS integration: we have a step-by-step sample (attached KMS_integration_sample.md) that shows creating a CMK in AWS KMS, granting Redwood's service principal access via a key policy, and configuring the account to reference the CMK ARN. For GCP KMS the pattern is similar with IAM bindings.
- HSM/on-prem: supported in Private deployments. For hosted customers we can integrate with CloudHSM (AWS) or HSM-backed KMS instances. For full on-prem HSMs we recommend a Private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and we can connect to the HSM over a secure channel.
- FIPS: Redwood itself leverages the crypto primitives of the underlying KMS/HSM. If a customer requires FIPS-validated cryptography, we need to select a FIPS-validated KMS/HSM provider and document the configuration. We should add a line in the MSA stating that key material is customer-owned and that Redwood will not export CMKs.

Action items for our side: Nikhil (infra) to join the deep-dive to cover architecture, and Security to provide a short note on FIPS options.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment (internal): KMS_integration_sample.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up (PayWise)

Amit — thanks for the quick read.

We can absolutely share the integration steps (attached) and Nikhil will join the tech deep-dive to cover HSM/private deployment options and regional availability. Brief answers now:
- KMS samples: attached (AWS/GCP). The flow shows how you create a CMK, grant Redwood principle access, and reference the CMK ARN/ID in the account config.
- HSM/on-prem: supported via Private deployments; CloudHSM supported for Dedicated. We'll outline the network and trust model in the deep-dive.
- FIPS: we'll surface FIPS-capable KMS/HSM provider options and include the relevant attestations in the follow-up pack.
- Data residency: we can provision serving and log storage in specific cloud regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1). There are no model-serving feature differences by region, but we will call out any region-specific compliance notes in the doc pack.

Proposed deep-dive times (PT): Tue 3/2 10:00–10:45 or Wed 3/3 14:00–14:45. I'll send a calendar invite for Tue 3/2 10:00 PT.

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_Options.pdf, SOC2_Audit_Report.pdf, KMS_integration_sample.md
